signal: Your team must cross an open area held by enemies, a teammate says their smoke is back in about 5 to 10 seconds, and there is still enough time on the clock.
decision: Freeze and hold your angles until the smoke is up, then walk out together behind it.
why: A few seconds of waiting costs nothing when the clock allows it, and crossing without cover hands the holders free kills.
mistakeToAvoid: Walking out one by one without utility because the round feels urgent when it is not yet.

source.topic: late round push when a smoke is seconds away

title: Attacking eco against rifles
signal: Your team has pistols or light buys and the defenders have rifles.
decision: Group four or five together, move quietly as you get close so they do not hear the stack, and swing at the same time or right behind one teammate so the first contact is traded and a rifle is picked up.
why: Pistols lose single duels against rifles. Only simultaneous close swings win them.
mistakeToAvoid: Each player takes their own angle and dies alone to a rifle, giving the defenders free kills and ult points.

source.topic: attacking eco against rifles

title: A favourite old execute meets a Vyse
signal: Your team is about to run a fast run out strat that you made before the enemy had Vyse, and Vyse is on the defending side.
decision: Find or bait the Vyse setups that cover the run out first, or pick a hit that avoids them. Do not count on the old timing.
why: Her setups stop players running out of the site entrance, which the old strat never had to handle.
mistakeToAvoid: Running the same execute and getting stuck at the run out with the site still unplanted.

source.topic: a favourite old execute meets a vyse

title: Diamond aim, Diamond rank
signal: Your aim in an aim test looks Ascendant or better but your rank is Platinum or Diamond, and your deaths often come from peeking an angle again or taking a duel no teammate can trade.
decision: Stop adding aim work. Review your deaths for the fight you chose, and cut repeat peeks and untradeable duels first.
why: Players whose aim already looks Ascendant but who sit at Platinum or Diamond lose rounds on over peeking and bad fights, so decisions, not aim, separate the ranks.
mistakeToAvoid: Grinding more aim training to fix what is a fight selection problem.

source.topic: diamond aim, diamond rank

title: Attack, a known Odin hold on the planned site, switch early
signal: Before the hit, your team has information that an enemy Odin is set up in a known strong position on the site you planned to take (here A tree), and nobody has died yet.
decision: As the caller, say the planned site will be hard and switch all five to the other site at once. Run it together and keep the ultimate in reserve unless it is needed.
why: A heavy machine gun in a set position wins the first contacts cheaply. Changing the target costs only a few seconds while all five are alive and on the same page.
mistakeToAvoid: Sticking with the planned site because it was the plan, and feeding the first two players into the known hold.

source.topic: attack, a known odin hold on the planned site, switch early

title: Anti eco lost to one lone walk into a site, then the reset round
signal: You won pistol, the enemy is saving with pistols and SMGs, and one teammate walks alone onto a site with nobody within trade distance.
decision: Stay together on the anti eco so the saving team never gets an isolated kill. Once the round is lost anyway, do not blame: the next round run a simple committed plan together with confidence (here a five player A rush), which won.
why: The lone death gave the enemy a free rifle and the information to fight together, which is exactly how an eco wins. The next round only needs the team back on the same page.
mistakeToAvoid: Spreading out on an anti eco because the round feels free, then tilting at the teammate and splitting up again the next round.

source.topic: anti eco lost to one lone walk into a site, then the reset round

title: Haven attack, a C rush stopped at the choke, fall back to the lurker
signal: Your rush meets a blind, a molotov and a recon dart at the choke and you cannot get through, while your lurker is alive on the other side of the map.
decision: Back off rather than forcing the choke. Reason that the defenders who just used that utility are probably three at that site, run to your lurker and hit the far site together.
why: The defense just spent its utility and in ranked will often over rotate toward the fight it just had, which leaves the other site light.
mistakeToAvoid: Forcing through the choke into active utility one player at a time.

source.topic: haven attack, a c rush stopped at the choke, fall back to the lurker

title: Haven defense, site lost to a rush, coordinate a four player retake
signal: One defender died on the site, the anchor fell back, the attackers own the site and four of you are alive.
decision: Each survivor says in one line what they will use (the controller a smoke and a blind, the initiator a dart, the duelist an entry) and you go in together on one call.
why: Ranked attackers on a site are often uncoordinated too, so a retake where four abilities are stated and timed together usually wins.
mistakeToAvoid: Four survivors peeking the site one by one from different places with no shared plan.

source.topic: haven defense, site lost to a rush, coordinate a four player retake

title: Ascent defense, an unholdable five player A execute, retake from three lanes
signal: Your A players say the site cannot be held against the execute coming in, and the attackers are using a lot of utility to take it.
decision: The A controller gives up the site and plays for the retake, two players come through mid and the link toward the side of A, and the rest come from the usual back site entrance, so the retake arrives from three directions instead of two.
why: The attackers spent most of their utility on the execute and now must watch three lanes, so you hold both a utility advantage and a lane advantage.
mistakeToAvoid: Dying on the site trying to hold an execute that cannot be held, or retaking from the two usual entrances only.

source.topic: ascent defense, an unholdable five player a execute, retake from three lanes

title: Retake with a numbers lead, group on spawn and go together
signal: You are up in numbers, the attackers are on the site and some may be trying to leave or save an Operator.
decision: Group the survivors at one spot, wait for the last teammate only while the spike timer still leaves time to reach the spike and finish the 7 second defuse, break the enemy wall together and retake as one. If the enemy holding the Operator tries to save it, hunt him.
why: A numbers lead is only an advantage if the bodies arrive together. A saved Operator is damage to your next round.
mistakeToAvoid: Trickling into the site one at a time because you are ahead, and letting the Operator walk away.

source.topic: retake with a numbers lead, group on spawn and go together

title: Last attacker against a defender chasing an ace
signal: You are the last attacker alive, the spike is planted, and the last defender has just made three or more kills in the round.
decision: Do not rush the spike or peek a known angle. Stay hidden near the spike, expect the defender to come looking for you before tapping, listen for a reload, then jiggle out and swing on the reload.
why: A defender on a multi kill run often hunts for the last kill before tapping, so time is on your side, and the reload is the moment their gun cannot answer.
mistakeToAvoid: Lower ranked players peek the defender straight away into a full magazine, or leave the spike area so the defender can tap freely.

source.topic: last attacker against a defender chasing an ace

title: Swung while planting with little time left
signal: You have started the plant, an enemy appears and shoots, and the round timer shows only a few seconds more than a plant needs.
decision: Count first: if your time to kill plus the 4 second plant fits in the timer, cancel, win the duel, and press plant the instant the enemy dies. If it does not fit, the round is lost either way, so take whichever line gives a chance.
why: Holding the plant while being shot loses the duel. Cancelling without time to replant loses the round. The clock decides.
mistakeToAvoid: Keeping the plant held while getting shot, or cancelling and then hesitating before replanting.

source.topic: swung while planting with little time left

title: Last defender hiding until the plant sound
signal: One attacker is left, holding the spike, and you have not seen them. The round timer is under about 25 seconds.
decision: Stay hidden on site and do not go looking. Wait for the plant sound to give you the location and the timing, then play the defuse or the fight from the angle you pick.
why: The attacker must make noise to plant before time runs out, so you get the information without taking a risk. Going to find them lets them choose the duel.
mistakeToAvoid: Pushing out to find the attacker and giving them a free first shot, or making noise that tells them which plant spot is safe.

source.topic: last defender hiding until the plant sound

title: Retake with a smoke coming and time on the spike
signal: The spike is down, your team has the numbers, and your controller says a smoke is ready in about 2 seconds.
decision: Call slow down, wait for the smoke, then go in together with each player calling the angle they take. Nobody needs a hero play.
why: With time and numbers, grouping and using the smoke turns the retake into trades. Trickling in lets the post-plant win one duel at a time.
mistakeToAvoid: The first player to arrive peeks alone before the smoke, dies, and turns a numbers advantage into an even fight.

source.topic: retake with a smoke coming and time on the spike

title: Enemy controller out of smokes
signal: You have counted the enemy controller use every smoke charge, or their wall is down, and a teammate calls they have no smokes.
decision: Commit now: swing the angle the smoke would have blocked, or push the site, before abilities come back or another player arrives.
why: Without smokes the enemy cannot cut your line of sight or slow the push, so this is the cheapest moment to win the space.
mistakeToAvoid: Waiting anyway, which gives the enemy time to rotate players in, or never tracking the smoke count at all.

source.topic: enemy controller out of smokes

title: Team gone quiet after losing several rounds
signal: Your team has lost three or more rounds in a row, comms have gone quiet, and players are dying alone without a trade.
decision: Reset with one simple plan: fight in pairs, double swing every contact, say what you see and what you throw. Do not add a new complicated strat.
why: Quiet, scared play produces lone deaths. Pairs and talking are the quickest way back to trades and even fights.
mistakeToAvoid: Blaming, going silent, or calling a fancy new plan the team has never run.

source.topic: team gone quiet after losing several rounds

title: Outnumbered with no info in a round you want
signal: You are alone against three or more, or two against four, with no call or utility showing any enemy in the last few seconds, and the spike state gives you no realistic win (on attack not planted with little time left, on defence planted with too little time to defuse).
decision: Save the rifle, break line of sight, hide off the likely paths and survive the round.
why: Without information the clutch is close to hopeless, and dying also loses the gun for the next round, so the loss compounds.
mistakeToAvoid: Hunting blind for a hero clutch because the round feels important, losing both round and rifle.

source.topic: outnumbered with no info in a round you want

title: Spike down with a two player lead
signal: The spike is planted and the kill feed shows you up 5v3 or 4v2.
decision: Hold the smokes and the angles onto the spike. Do not chase kills away from site. Wait for the defenders to walk into you or tap the spike.
why: The timer is on your side. Every chase gives a defender a fair duel and a way to even the numbers.
mistakeToAvoid: Pushing out to hunt the remaining defenders, dying one at a time, and turning a won round into a retake.

source.topic: spike down with a two player lead

title: Enemy initiator has no flashes left
signal: You saw or heard the enemy flasher spend every flash this round and a teammate calls it.
decision: Hold and peek that side more aggressively, but only for flashes that cannot come back this round, since some agents' flashes recharge or can be picked back up, and still respect smokes and other unspent utility.
why: Most of the risk of holding an angle close or swinging wide comes from a flash. Once it is gone the duel is a pure aim and position duel.
mistakeToAvoid: Playing every angle as if the enemy still has full utility, giving up space for free.

source.topic: enemy initiator has no flashes left

title: Retake swing timed to a teammate's reveal
signal: Your initiator says they will reveal or recon the site.
decision: Hold just off the angle, say you are waiting for it, and swing the moment the reveal lands, together with the next player on a countdown.
why: The reveal tells you who is where for a short window. Swinging into it with a partner turns the info into kills and trades.
mistakeToAvoid: Swinging before the reveal because you are impatient, or after it has faded, so the util is wasted.

source.topic: retake swing timed to a teammate's reveal

title: Lost attack half, what to fix
signal: Several rounds were lost to first deaths no teammate traded.
decision: Keep the strategy and fix one thing: play close enough to each other that every death is traded.
why: Untraded deaths are a spacing error, not a strategy error. Rewriting the plan adds confusion.
mistakeToAvoid: Throwing out every default and trying new strats after one bad half.

source.topic: lost attack half, what to fix

title: Spike time shorter than a defuse
signal: The spike is past its fast beeps by a few seconds, so fewer than 7 seconds are left, and the defenders have not reached the half.
decision: Stop peeking and stay alive. The round is already won.
why: No defuse can finish, so a duel only risks your life and your gun for nothing.
mistakeToAvoid: Swinging for an extra kill and dying, losing the gun for the save.

source.topic: spike time shorter than a defuse

title: Operator Chamber holding a main
signal: A teammate calls the enemy Chamber with an Operator playing off a main entrance.
decision: Get back from the lane, then either take the site with utility that blocks his line or go elsewhere.
why: He can take the first shot and teleport out, so any dry peek is a free kill for him.
mistakeToAvoid: Peeking the Operator wide on your own, losing a player for nothing.

source.topic: operator chamber holding a main

title: Overtime after a thrown lead
signal: The map has gone to overtime, often after rounds your team feels it should have closed.
decision: Reset fully, talk only about the next round's plan and buy, and play it at normal pace.
why: Overtime rounds come in pairs and each one can end the map, and everyone gets the same overtime credits, so carrying regret into them only leads to forced plays.
mistakeToAvoid: Arguing about earlier rounds or forcing hero plays to make up for them.

source.topic: overtime after a thrown lead

title: Man advantage late in the round
signal: The kill feed shows your team up by at least one player, and the round timer (or spike timer) still has time the enemy has to spend to win.
decision: Call the count, tell the team to wait, and hold the angles the enemy must cross. Take a fight only when they show.
why: The side up in numbers with time to spare loses only by giving away duels. Waiting makes the outnumbered side walk into crossfires.
mistakeToAvoid: The first player to feel confident swings for another kill alone, dies untraded and turns 4v3 into an even fight.

source.topic: man advantage late in the round

title: Flash and paired swing on an entry
signal: A teammate with a flash says they are flashing your angle, and a second teammate is next to you.
decision: Count the swing (three, two, one), peek as the flash pops, and have the second player swing straight after so any death is traded.
why: The flash only wins the duel during its short window, and a second swinger turns the first contact into a two on one.
mistakeToAvoid: Peeking before the flash pops or a beat after it fades, or swinging alone while the partner waits around the corner.

source.topic: flash and paired swing on an entry

title: Between rounds after a teammate's mistake
signal: The last round was lost on a visible individual mistake and the team is in the buy phase.
decision: Say something supportive to the player who made it, then state the plan for the next round. The review of the mistake waits until after the match.
why: A team that stays focused on each other and on what it controls plays the next round better than one that replays the mistake, and blame in the buy phase costs the next round's focus.
mistakeToAvoid: Replaying the mistake in comms, or going silent and playing the next round alone.

source.topic: between rounds after a teammate's mistake

title: Gekko about to plant the spike
signal: Your team has the site, you hold the spike as Gekko, and Wingman is available.
decision: Send Wingman to plant and use the time to move to a strong post-plant angle yourself, then pick up the globule later.
why: The plant no longer needs a body, so one more player is in position for the retake fight.
mistakeToAvoid: Sending Wingman to plant and then standing still next to it, a habit even Immortal players have.

source.topic: gekko about to plant the spike

title: You were spotted first and your teammate is next to you
signal: You just got scanned, missed your first jiggle, or an enemy clearly turned to your angle, and a teammate is close by on another angle onto the same enemy.
decision: Do not re peek. Keep jiggling and making yourself a threat so the enemy stays aimed at you, while your teammate swings the enemy who is not ready for him. The moment he fires, re swing for the trade without waiting to see the enemy turn.
why: The player holding attention faces a ready crosshair. The other player gets the free duel, and the turn to face him gives you your own window.
mistakeToAvoid: Wide swinging again because you know where the enemy is, or fully hiding so the enemy turns onto your teammate's lane.

source.topic: you were spotted first and your teammate is next to you

title: Lurking while your team fakes loudly on the other site
signal: Your team is making loud pressure on one site, you sit silently in a spot close to the defenders' rotate path, and you hear running or a teleport heading toward your team's noise.
decision: Call the rotate at once so the team turns back to the weakened site, and stay silent yourself. Then take the fastest timing on the players left behind, who now have to respect every option.
why: Many defenders rotate at full run on a fake. Once the team freezes and goes quiet, the remaining defenders must cover everything and the lurker gets the punish.
mistakeToAvoid: The lurker making his own noise, or the team continuing the fake after the rotate is heard.

source.topic: lurking while your team fakes loudly on the other site

title: Choosing the plant spot when your post plant player is in a lane
signal: You are planting, and a teammate holds a lane outside site (a link or main) that will be your main threat on the defuse.
decision: Plant in a spot that is visible from that lane, even if it is not the most tucked default, so your teammate can deny the defuse without moving.
why: A plant hidden in the corner forces your team to walk straight across the site or wide swing onto an angle disadvantage to stop the defuse.
mistakeToAvoid: Planting in the safest looking corner by habit and then having nobody who can see the spike.

source.topic: choosing the plant spot when your post plant player is in a lane

title: Your defence is stacked where the attackers are pushing
signal: Three or four defenders are in the area the attackers are hitting, and the attackers are walking toward the entrance.
decision: Hide and hold the utility. Let them walk in as if the area is free, then fight them inside your setup with your utility and crossfires.
why: Stalling utility at the entrance only delays a team you outnumber. Letting them in gives you the numbers fight you want.
mistakeToAvoid: Throwing every stun, blind and recon at the choke, which uses everything and lets them retreat and come back later.

title: Placing the execute smokes as a Platinum controller
signal: You are throwing your default execute smokes, the team will plant and play post plant, and you cannot say why one of the smokes is where it is.
decision: Place each smoke so a defender coming out has one predictable edge, leave the link defenders rotate through unsmoked so your post plant can kill them, and keep at least one teammate on the other lane if the team goes through mid.
why: A smoke with a straight exit line makes crosshair placement easy, and an open rotate lane gives your post plant kills.
mistakeToAvoid: Throwing a smoke because someone once suggested it, which can block your own post plant or let a defender come out either side.

title: Holding a molly while the attackers stop their push
signal: The attackers used a camera and a molly to clear a corner, then there was no flash, no recon and no further steps.
decision: Keep your molly ready in case they take the timing, and do not throw it once the push dries up. Save it for the real hit.
why: No follow up utility after a clear means they are not committing. A molly thrown now is gone for when they are.
mistakeToAvoid: Throwing the molly into the choke on the first sound, as lower ranked defenders do.

title: A solo timing through a lane with no pressure elsewhere
signal: You want to take a first timing alone through a side lane, and nobody on your team has shown, made noise or used utility anywhere else yet.
decision: Wait until a teammate pulls attention to another site or lane, then take the timing. If nobody does, do not take it alone.
why: With no attention pulled, the defender on that lane is aimed at it and holding you. The timing only works when he is looking elsewhere.
mistakeToAvoid: Taking the first timing alone and dying to a hold, giving the defence a free man advantage.

title: Defending against a composition without flashes
signal: The enemy has no flash, for example a Raze, Neon and Cypher comp.
decision: Plan setups on open long range high low angles and hold the edges of smokes. They have no way to blind you off the angle, so they have to walk through.
why: Without flashes they cannot blind you off a long angle, so long open duels and smoke edge holds favour you, but Neon's Relay Bolt and other concusses still punish close corners, and Raze utility clears them.
mistakeToAvoid: Playing the same close corner setups you would use against a flash heavy comp.

title: Defusing or holding a corner against a Hush with Displacement
signal: An enemy Hush is alive with Displacement available (it resets every two kills), and you are about to defuse or are holding a corner she can throw at.
decision: Hold from a spot away from walls, boxes and teammates, and before a full defuse, tap or fake to draw the pull out first, so a pull drags you through open air instead of slamming you into something.
why: Displacement pulls every player near its center toward it and concusses anyone pulled into a surface or another player, and dragging defusers off the spike is one of its main uses.
mistakeToAvoid: Committing to a full defuse beside a wall or box, or stacking next to a teammate, while her Displacement is up.

title: Solo Jett entry into a site with no team utility
signal: You cleared the outer approach and saw nobody, and no teammate has used a flash, smoke or recon for your entry.
decision: Smoke the angle you cannot clear at the site edge, dash in while turning to clear one side, take cover behind your smoke rather than in the open middle of site, and wait for the teammate behind you to draw the first fight, then swing on the defender who turned toward him.
why: An empty approach means the defenders are on site. Dashing and turning clears one angle for free, and waiting in smoke lets the second player's fight pull the defenders' attention away from you.
mistakeToAvoid: Dashing blind into the middle of site and shooting immediately, alone, so the defense trades nothing and kills you first.

title: Stopping a Jett or Neon execute with a KAY/O knife
signal: You hear the attackers stack and make noise just outside the site, about to commit.
decision: Throw the knife onto them before they come out, so they cannot use utility to support the entry, then molly or swing the lone duelist who comes in while your controller's smoke or a teammate holds the other side.
why: Suppression takes away every attacker's support utility at once, so the duelist enters with nothing behind him.
mistakeToAvoid: Saving the knife until they are already on site, when the support utility has already gone out.

title: Executing a site with smoke, two mollies, a dash and a flash
signal: Your team has a controller, an entry and two molly sources ready for the same site.
decision: Smoke first, then the entry dashes into the smoke and checks both sides, mollies deny the angle that peeks the entry and the defenders' rotate path, then the flash pops beyond the smoke and the entry swings the nearest defender. With flashes left, flash again and fight together, and without them, trade together out of the smoke.
why: Each step protects the next. The entry waiting in smoke for the flash avoids a blind fight, and moving out together guarantees trades.
mistakeToAvoid: Flashing before the entry is in place, or the entry swinging before the flash, so utility and fight never line up.
